title: The ending of To Live and Die in LA

commenti.body:
They're just pieces in a system. You take one out, someone will fill that place no matter what. That he had a conscience before and then goes "bad" is *exactly* the point.

It's one of the great cynical endings, and anti-buddy movie almost right when buddy-movies were just getting started.

Glad you enjoyed it, and that the ending still had punch forty years later.

That last scene always felt very tacked-on to me, as if the studio thought the audience wouldn't understand that Vukovich had been set down the same dark path as his partner unless he literally starts wearing his clothes and shacking up with his girl. 
I think it's heavyhandedness obscured the subtler parts of his arc in a candle-to-the-sun sort of way, not giving you a chance or a reason to look for the finer threads of the story to weave together afterwards.
